messages.subject: NaNs, non positive-probability errors and key detection functions
parts:
Hello group,

I'm using gdistsamp to model abundance (using 2 covariates) and am running into error issues with a top fit model. Specifically:

> gdistsamp(lambdaformula = ~stnd.ag + stnd.well, phiformula = ~1, 
    pformula = ~1, data = umfsp1, keyfun = "exp", output = "density", 
    unitsOut = "ha", mixture = "NB")

1: In dnbinom(x, mu = lambda, size = exp(pars[nP])) : NaNs produced

Based on past posts, I attempted to provide start values and modify the maximum integration value (K) in the model but I receive the same error message. 

To troubleshoot, I continued to parametric bootstrap the model (then nonparboot) and I quickly receive this error:

> pbSpr2 <- parboot(spring1fin$ag_well,nsim=2,report=1)
t0 = 4.992748e+17 

Error in rmultinom(1, N, prob = cp.it) : non-positive probability

To me, I interpret this as negative abundance estimates are created by the bootstrap (probably wrong) but my t0 is huge! So huge, I believe that is probably the issue. I have approx. 710 observations over 3 seasons. I investigated my detection histogram for spikes, etc. but everything looks OK despite the use of the Exponential key function in gdistsamp. I tried further truncation and playing with distance breaks but Exp. NB continues to be the top model.

Buckland et al. (2001) cautions the use of the Exponential key function. My next best key (delta AICc 55.12, wi = 0.00) is the Half Normal NB which seems make the error messages stop and the log(lambda, phi, p and a) are fairly similar. Simply dropping to a "better-behaved" model without trying to address the Exp. error issue in the function itself seems, well, wrong.

Has anyone dealt with this issue and if so, is there a way to deal with these types of errors in the gdistsamp or bootstrap functions while retaining the best fit key function/distribution?

I apologize if this is not strictly an unmarked/gdistsamp issue.

Thanks for your time, Erik
